The code will not work as written. The most critical bug is in `process_request`: it iterates over `request.post` directly with `for line in request.post:`. However, `request.post` is an **async method (coroutine)**, not an iterable. You must `await request.post()` (which returns a MultiDict of form fields), or better, `await request.text()` since the body is a plain list of URLs, one per line. As written, this raises `TypeError: 'coroutine' object is not iterable`, so the handler crashes and no report is ever produced.

Additionally, `request.post()` parses the body as form-encoded data, which is the wrong way to read a raw newline-delimited URL list; `await request.text()` then splitting on newlines is what the task requires.

A secondary issue: `session.get(url, timeout=10)` passes an `int` for the timeout, which modern versions of aiohttp reject with a `TypeError` (they require a `ClientTimeout` object). This would be caught by the bare `except`, turning every request into `Error`, which is also incorrect behavior.

Because the primary handler fails to read the body at all, the program does not accomplish the task.

There is no `writelines` method on the handler, so this raises `AttributeError: 'ReportHandler' object has no attribute 'writelines'`, and the HTML response is never actually sent to the client. Exception handling conflates HTTP errors with request failures. `urllib.error.HTTPError` is a subclass of `urllib.error.URLError`, so catching only `urllib.error.URLError` also catches non-2xx responses (e.g., 404, 500). The task requires recording the numeric HTTP status code whenever a request completes, so a 404 must be recorded as "404", not "Error". As written, any URL returning an error status is recorded as "Error", which contradicts the requirement.
